newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on speculative buying.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended Monday up from New York's previous close on speculative buying in a volatile market, compounded by strong palladium, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$342.50/343.00 an ounce against New York's US$341.10/60 close on Friday.
Prices went up on speculative buying after rumours swirled in the market about a fund planning to buy a large amount of gold, dealers said.
"It was a very volatile market," said one dealer.
Prices also inched up on stronger palladium, sources said.
Bullion had held steady in the morning session on slight buying from Japan, but market sentiment had been mixed and prices range-bound.
Dealers noted average physical demand, but said that physical buyers were taking advantage of arbitrage opportunities to sell local Hong Kong tael gold and buy spot loco London.
Bullion was seen trending higher overnight to test $343.50, dealers said.
Local gold ended HK$13 higher at HK$3,171 a tael.
The carry over charge from the Chinese Gold and Silver
Exchange Society rose to -6.00 from its previous fix at -8.00
